summary: Morgan James, a narrator in a fiction novel, phones the owner's son at a remote facility to ask whether Steve Abrams is staying there; he says no one by that name is present. She then considers calling the embassy, decides to wait until 6 A.M., and turns to the facility's computers to uncover the real purpose behind the research. Among the files she finds a list labeled QUETZAL containing six women's names, each marked 'terminated', including S. Crenshaw and her own name, M. James, which alarms her.
one_line: Morgan James phones a remote facility looking for Steve Abrams, then discovers a file listing terminated women that includes her own name.
key_facts: Morgan James calls the owner's son at the facility to ask whether a Steve Abrams is staying there now.
The owner's son is trying his best to learn English and greets her with 'Hey, que pasa, Senora James.'
The son replies that 'No, nobody by that name stays here.'
Morgan James replaces the handset, grateful that at least the phone still works.
Morgan James decides not to call the embassy yet because she cannot risk using up her opening shot with the graveyard shift.
She hopes that by 6 A.M. somebody with authority to do something will be at the embassy.
Morgan James is a Mac fan who hates Windows and has to proceed by trial and error on the terminal.
She finds an index of files that includes a long list of names and plant-extract categories, which suggests research on the local flora.
Toward the end of the alphabetical list she finds a file named QUETZAL containing six names of women.
The six names are organized by dates about a year apart, and each entry is marked 'terminated'.
The name next to the last is S. Crenshaw, who is also marked 'terminated'.
The bottom name on the list is M. James, which is Morgan James's own name.
Morgan James notes that she has not been 'terminated', 'not yet'.
Morgan James suspects that the facility is called Quetzal Manor and that the women may have come there for fertility treatment.
